input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

stage_control_options.title: Stage control options
stage_control_options.description: Where a run should stop short of the whole pipeline.

stop_after.description: Run only as far as this stage, then finish and report.
stop_after.help_text: The stages are the pipeline's own boundaries, not carmack's command names: `barcodes`, `umis` and `targets` each stop after the matching step of the read-preparation chain, `readprep` stops after `prepare-reads`, and `gate` stops after the arm fan-out and its gate report, so no aligner runs and no reference is needed. Unset, the whole pipeline runs. MultiQC still assembles from the stages that ran, so every stop point leaves a usable report behind.

read_preparation_options.title: Read preparation options
read_preparation_options.description: Options controlling how carmack reads the library layout and prepares raw reads.

chemistry.description: Name of the carmack chemistry describing the read structure of the library. The allowed list tracks the vendored carmack build.
chemistry.help_text: The chemistry declares the barcode, UMI and target index layout of R1, and is required by every carmack read-preparation stage. The `enum` mirrors the chemistries registered in `external/carmack/carmack/chemistry/__init__.py` at the pinned submodule, so it has to be updated alongside a carmack bump that adds one.

carmack_fast.description: Skip carmack's local alignment fallback during barcode extraction.
carmack_fast.help_text: Passes `--fast` to `carmack extract-barcodes`, dropping the third matching stage. Faster, at the cost of the barcodes only local alignment recovers.

arm_gate_options.title: Arm gate options
arm_gate_options.description: Thresholds deciding which per-arm units of work proceed past read preparation.

min_arm_reads.description: Reads an arm must carry to be processed.
min_arm_reads.help_text: Each sample fans out into one arm per target index carmack's prepare-reads report accounts for, plus the scRNA (`NONE`) arm. An arm carrying fewer reads than this is warned about, recorded in `pipeline_info/arm_gate.tsv` as `FAIL` and dropped; its sibling arms and every other sample are unaffected. The minimum of 1 means an arm that received no read at all can never proceed.

fail_on_no_arms.description: Stop the run when every arm of a sample falls below `--min_arm_reads`.
fail_on_no_arms.help_text: By default such a sample is warned about and dropped, so one bad library cannot discard the completed work of a large run. Set this when a sample losing every arm should instead fail the run; the error names the sample.

trimming_options.title: Trimming options
trimming_options.description: Adapter and quality trimming applied to each arm that cleared the gate.

skip_trimming.description: Align and quantify the reads prepare-reads wrote, untrimmed.
skip_trimming.help_text: Both arms are trimmed with fastp by default, against an adapter FASTA derived from the sequences the selected `--chemistry` declares. Set this to bypass fastp on both arms; every downstream step still runs, so the run produces the same outputs from untrimmed reads. Trimming can leave an arm below `--min_arm_reads`, in which case it is dropped and recorded as `FAIL_TRIM`; with this set no arm can be dropped after the gate.

deduplication_options.title: Deduplication options
deduplication_options.description: Duplicate removal applied to the scTIP arm's alignments.

skip_linear_dedup.description: Leave the scTIP arm's alignments as `umi_tools dedup` left them.
skip_linear_dedup.help_text: The scTIP arm deduplicates twice. `umi_tools dedup --paired` collapses PCR duplicates, keying on the UMI together with the coordinates of both mates. It cannot collapse linear-amplification duplicates: the copies linear amplification makes of one template all share R1's 5' end but terminate at different points, so they carry different mate ends and different UMIs and read as distinct molecules. That shared start is what carmack's linear-dedup pass keys on — per cell, R1's strand-aware fragment position alone — keeping the highest-scoring pair of each group. Set this to stop after the UMI pass; the arm still emits a BAM and its index, and `samtools stats` still reports on it.

scrna_arm_options.title: scRNA arm options
scrna_arm_options.description: Options for quantifying the scRNA arm with STARsolo.

solo_features.description: Genomic features STARsolo counts UMIs against, space-separated.
solo_features.help_text: One or more of `Gene`, `GeneFull`, `GeneFull_ExonOverIntron`, `GeneFull_Ex50pAS`, `SJ` and `Velocyto`, separated by spaces — STARsolo writes one count matrix per feature and `--soloFeatures` takes a list, so this does too. `GeneFull` counts reads overlapping a gene's introns as well as its exons. This is Tn5-derived multiome material, where intronic reads are a large fraction of real signal, so exon-only `Gene` counting discards most of it. `Gene` is always produced in addition to whatever is asked for here, because the report and the per-arm run summary are read off it.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`. 

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

fasta.help_text: Required whenever `--genome` is not given and an arm has no prebuilt index: the scRNA arm builds its STAR index from this and `--gtf`, and the scTIP arm builds its bowtie2 index from this alone.

gtf.description: Path to GTF gene annotation file.
gtf.help_text: Required alongside `--fasta` whenever `--star_index` is not given: STARsolo can only assign a read to a gene against an annotation, and that annotation is baked into the index as it is built.

star_index.description: Path to a prebuilt STAR index directory.
star_index.help_text: Skips index building for the scRNA arm. The index must have been built from the annotation you intend to count against, since STARsolo reads that annotation out of the index rather than off `--gtf`.

bowtie2_index.description: Path to a prebuilt bowtie2 index directory.
bowtie2_index.help_text: Skips index building for the scTIP arm. This is the directory `bowtie2-build` wrote, holding the `*.bt2` files, rather than a path prefix.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
